summary: A helper that wraps the Redis connection with simple methods for reading, writing, deleting, and hash storage.
purpose: Lets features store and read short-lived data without handling Redis details.
why: The header calls it a cache wrapper, which is the stated purpose.
how: 1) Each method passes the request to the Redis connection. 2) Writes can include an expiry time in seconds. 3) The delete-by-prefix method finds every key that starts with a given text and deletes them. 4) On shutdown the connection is closed.
inputs: Key names, values, optional expiry in seconds, and hash field names.
outputs: Stored values, returned values, or nothing.
risks: delete-by-prefix uses a command that scans all keys, which can slow Redis on large data. Values are stored as plain text, so any sensitive data stored here is unencrypted.
debug: If a read returns nothing, the key may be missing or expired, so check the expiry time and the spelling of the key. If Redis is slow, check whether delete-by-prefix is being used on a large set of keys.
